guard_streams.source: Mobile coverage, technical and planning advice
guard_streams.write_limit: Technical, planning and mast-enquiry guidance routes issues to the relevant organisations. It does not verify fixed-broadband service at a selected parcel.

facts.detail: Ofcom published the mobile technical and planning advice on 6 March 2024.
The page provides advice and links for mobile coverage, technical and planning enquiries.
It links advice on mast siting policy, relevant legislation and further information.
It links Ofcom advice on cellular coverage.
Construction or utility works affecting a site should be reported to the relevant mobile operator.
Service outages or loss of coverage should be reported to the relevant operator.
Damage, noise, alarms, access, ownership and lease issues are directed to the operator.
Site-sharing and local-planning-authority enquiries are also directed to the operator.
MobileUK is identified as a central industry contact point.
The page notes published EMF measurements within limits and a chargeable Ofcom survey service.

guard_streams.write_limit: 5G EMF safety measurements concern exposure limits and tested mast locations. They do not establish broadband serviceability or parcel speed.

facts.detail: Ofcom published the 5G safety feature on 16 June 2023.
The feature describes twice-monthly testing in Belfast.
Two Ofcom spectrum engineers carry out the Belfast tests.
Testing uses an antenna on a tripod connected to a spectrum analyser.
The engineers test four city locations for around 15 minutes each.
The testing batch covered more than 60 sites in 20 UK towns and cities.
The feature references ICNIRP exposure guidelines formally recognised by WHO.
UKHSA is identified as the UK lead for public-health advice on radio waves.
Ofcom reports the highest observed level at about 7.1% of the ICNIRP reference level and the next highest at 1.5%.
Ofcom states that testing will continue as 5G deployment and take-up develop.

guard_streams.write_limit: The evaluation plan describes programme design, data and counterfactual methods. It cannot establish current serviceability or measured speed for surrounding parcels.

facts.detail: BDUK published the Hubs Evaluation Plan on 15 August 2025.
BDUK commissioned an independent evaluation of the Hub intervention.
The intervention connects remote public buildings such as schools, GP surgeries and libraries.
Initial Hubs were delivered through the Rural Gigabit Connectivity programme from 2019 to 2022.
GigaHubs are delivered through Project Gigabit during 2022 to 2026.
The evaluation period runs from 2022 to 2027.
The plan covers remaining evaluation work from 2024 to 2027.
It sets out a theory of change, data collection, evaluation methods and implementation.
The plan states that £110 million of Project Gigabit funding was made available for Hubs.
The evaluation uses counterfactual analysis and propensity-score matching alongside qualitative evidence.

guard_streams.source: Buckinghamshire, Hertfordshire and East of Berkshire Public Review closure notice
guard_streams.write_limit: OMR/PR classifications, postcode maps and procurement redesign are subsidy-planning evidence. They do not prove current orderability or parcel-measured speed.

facts.detail: The closure notice was updated on 23 June 2026.
The Public Review ran from 4 February to 4 March 2022.
BDUK invited feedback from the public, businesses, ISPs and infrastructure operators.
The Public Review aimed to validate the preceding OMR.
Premises were classified White, Grey, Black or Under Review.
BDUK states that subsidy targets only premises designated White.
Postcodes are used for presentation and not to determine intervention areas for subsidy.
The published 2022 findings report 140,713 White premises.
A May 2026 redesign revised the contract to cover around 6,000 premises.
The redesigned contract is backed by £24.4 million of Project Gigabit investment.
